key_insight: Strong diagnostic performance did not ensure reliable downstream cancer-care reasoning, and dominant failure modes changed across care phases.
clinical_relevance: Evaluating medical AI across longitudinal care may reveal errors and omissions that isolated diagnostic benchmarks miss.
method: Built NPC-RubricBench from longitudinal nasopharyngeal carcinoma records across six care phases.
Scored 30 general-purpose and medical LLMs using patient-specific criteria restricted to decision-time evidence.
Varied prompt granularity to assess trade-offs in decision quality, evidence faithfulness, and safety adherence.
evidence_signal: The benchmark included 405 patients from two cancer centers, 941 patient-phase units, and 17,688 atomic criteria; explicit decision errors dominated staging at 48.2%, while omissions dominated initial work-up at 33.4% and follow-up at 30.4%.
watch_item: Results from one cancer type and two centers may not generalize to other settings, and benchmark performance does not establish clinical safety.
paper_title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
